mechanism: String.prototype builtins receive rope-tagged receivers and re-descend the rope tree on every call because none of zjs's three receiver-coercion boundaries linearizes. qjs linearizes once inside JS_ToStringInternal (JS_TAG_STRING_ROPE → js_linearize_string_rope, quickjs.c:13597-13598), which every String.prototype body hits via JS_ToStringCheckObject (e.g. js_string_charCodeAt, quickjs.c:45452), and the linearization mutates the rope node so revisits are O(1) (quickjs.c:4838-4857). zjs already owns the exact faithful adaptation — StringRope.flatten (string.zig:148-176) mutates the node in place (left=flat, right=undefined, depth=0) and is O(1) idempotent via flatString()/isLinearized() — but no string-builtin receiver path calls it: stringPrimitiveIndexRead (string_builtin_ops.zig:190) reads through the rope per call, and toStringForAnnexB (string_ops.zig:355) early-returns `value.dup()` because isString() (value.zig:319-320) is true for the string_rope tag, silently passing ropes through the very boundary that qjs uses to flatten. Fix: mirror qjs's tag split at all receiver-coercion fragments via one shared linearize helper, so 289,569 charCodeAt calls/run pay one materialization per distinct rope plus an O(1) check per revisit instead of an O(depth) pointer chase per call.

VERDICT: the claim survives, essentially at its stated magnitude — but for a sharper reason than the attribution recorded, and its bookkeeping premise ("10.76 zjs vs ~5.4 qjs") turns out to be accidentally right despite being derived from mismatched buckets.

(1) The spill is real and unconditional. Current binary (zig-out/bin/zjs, op_put_array_el @0x116ccf8; campaign binary saved in /tmp/pdfjs-attrib/zjs.dis @0x116ceb8, identical code shifted −0x40): entry executes `ldr x20,[x19,#-48]!` (obj word) then `ldp q1,q0,[x19,#16]` (key+value pair, 32B, via SIMD regs) → `stp q0,q1,[sp]` (frame spill) → `ldp x23,x22,[sp]` + `ldr x24,[sp,#24]` + `ldr x25,[sp,#16]` (scalar reloads). This runs on EVERY put_array_el — dense hit, sparse, typed, and cold exit alike — because LLVM hoists the operand-pair frame materialization above all branches (the slow legs need by-pointer operands: setOwnWritableDataProperty takes x4=sp value-ptr, putTypedArrayElementFast takes x4/x5 ptrs into the frame; src/exec/tailcall_dispatch.zig:3117-3186).

(2) Per-IP cycle evidence (campaign perf capture, /tmp/pdfjs-attrib/zjs-ip-counts.txt + zjs-a2l.txt, reconciles exactly: 110 samples × 0.78275 Mcyc/sample = 86.1 Mcyc N=8 = profile-absolute.json's 86.09): the q-spill cluster — 18 samples on `stp q0,q1,[sp]` (skid target of the ldp q operand load), 1 on the `ldp x` reload, 36 on the instruction immediately after it — totals 55/110 samples = **5.38 Mcyc/run**, i.e. the claimed 5.4 was per-IP-derived and reproduces. Regional breakdown: entry block 70 samples (6.85 Mcyc/run), everything else (dense arm 2, sparse 5, typed 18, epilogues 15) is minor. This is the opposite finding from the initial current-binary misread: I first mapped the saved IPs against today's build and got ~1 sample on the spill — but 0x12f7c90 addr2lines differently across builds, proving the saved capture is from the campaign binary; against the campaign binary's own layout the spill cluster dominates. The mechanism is a store-to-load-forwarding pathology: freshly-pushed operand-stack slots (GPR stores by preceding handlers) are read back through one 32-byte vector ldp q (multi-store-to-one-load, no forward on Neoverse), then the vector frame store is immediately re-read by GPR loads — a double forwarding-hostile round trip, ~6.6 cyc/op average over 0.816M ops/run (opcode-N2.txt: 1,631,799/2).

(3) qjs comparison is now like-for-like. qjs's OP_put_array_el arm (quickjs.c:19546-19594) loads only the words it needs as scalars (JS_VALUE_GET_TAG(sp[-3]) etc.), passes JSValues by value in registers to JS_SetPropertyValue on the slow path, and has no aggregate round trip. The original "~5.4 qjs" was actually JS_SetPropertyValue's 43.62/8=5.45 (wrong bucket — that's the analog of zjs's out-of-line helpers putTypedArrayElementFast 5.59 + putDense 1.75+0.17 Mcyc/run), but the corrected like-for-like comparison lands at the same excess by coincidence.

(4) Subset question: in the INSTRUCTION domain the q-spill is a small subset (~4-5 insn) of the confirmed 39-insn dense-write shell delta (132 vs 93). In the CYCLE domain it is mostly additional stall, not instruction retirement: 4-5 insn at zjs IPC ≈ 0.9 Mcyc/run, yet the cluster costs 5.4 — an IPC hole the insn accounting misses. The task's ceiling math (0.82M × 39 = 32 Minsn = 6.6 Mcyc) therefore UNDERSTATES what a full shell fix recovers on the entry side but the two budgets overlap: one edit (see fixDesign) removes both; do not sum 6.6 + 5.4. Total put_array_el family excess on pdfjs: zjs 18.27 (handler 10.76 + typed 5.59 + dense 1.75 + append 0.17) vs qjs ~10.3 (arm 4.89 + JS_SetPropertyValue 5.45) ≈ 8 Mcyc/run measured ceiling.

(5) Worth a knife? Not on pdfjs alone: 5.4 Mcyc at STLF-stall realization (this is a stall, the class ATTRIBUTION expects to convert; project realization 0.6-0.82 for stall/pointer-chase) → ~3-4 Mcyc/run ≈ 1% of the 388 Mcyc gap, ranked far behind splice (165), string-eq (32), dispatch shell (24.7), charCodeAt (9.8). fixDesign:
Faithful mirror of qjs:19546-19585 (OP_put_array_el keeps the dense arm fully inline and touches operands only as scalar words; slow legs go out of line with by-value handoff). Shape, using the project's proven cold-twin pattern ("LLVM csel 计算存储地址只 noinline 冷孪生能破"):

1. In op_put_array_el (src/exec/tailcall_dispatch.zig:3117-3186), restrict the hot body to the dense JS_CLASS_ARRAY arm, mirroring qjs:19552-19582 inline: load obj tag word, key tag word, and payload words as individual u64 scalar loads from the operand stack (never as 16-byte JSValue aggregate copies — that is what LLVM vectorizes into the ldp q/stp q round trip), check obj tag/isArray/int key, then inline the overwrite (`set_value`, qjs:19582) and append (qjs:19558-19580) bodies currently out-of-line in putDenseArrayElementOverwriteOwnedFast/AppendOwnedFast (array_ops.zig). This simultaneously removes the bl-pair from the dense path (the 39-insn shell delta's other half).
2. Move the sparse-array leg (fastArrayOwnIntElementSet → setOwnWritableDataProperty), the typed-array leg (putTypedArrayElementFast), and their free chains into one noinline cold-twin `op_put_array_el_slow(pc, sp, var_buf, vm)` that re-derives the operands from sp itself — exactly qjs's put_array_el_slow_path → JS_SetPropertyValue structure (qjs:19585-19592). With no by-pointer operand consumer left in the hot function, LLVM has no reason to materialize the frame copy; the 0x90 frame should shrink and the `stp q` must disappear from the hot prologue.
3. Liveness proof (mandatory): temporary counters in (a) hot dense overwrite arm, (b) hot append arm, (c) cold twin; run /tmp/pdfjs-attrib/runN.js N=1 and require a+b+c ≈ 0.816M/run with a+b > 0 (expect ~0.2M dense-ish, ~0.6M typed per the source comment at tailcall_dispatch.zig:3122-3126); plus objdump assert: no `stp q` in op_put_array_el before the first branch. Also run the navier-stokes zoo bench for the dense-arm counters.
4. Verification: perf stat -e instructions differential on runN.js (expect ~−3-5 Minsn/run on pdfjs from the dense-path bl removal; the stall win is cycles-only) and on navier-stokes (expect the bulk of 39 insn × dense-write volume).
